messages.content: Hypothetically, how might a daily warehouse stock report work? This is a discussion only; do not start or create a responsibility.

parts.text: Hypothetically, how might a daily warehouse stock report work? This is a discussion only; do not start or create a responsibility.

messages.content:
A daily warehouse stock report typically runs after the day’s inventory transactions are recorded. It combines opening balances with receipts, shipments, transfers, adjustments, and returns, then compares the calculated stock with any physical counts.

It might show:

- SKU, item description, and location
- Opening quantity, received, shipped, adjusted, and closing quantity
- Reorder threshold and low-stock flags
- Items with zero stock, unusual changes, or mismatches
- Report time and data source, so readers know how current it is

A scheduled process could generate it as a spreadsheet or dashboard, send it to warehouse and purchasing staff, and retain prior reports for trend checks. A good design also calls out missing or delayed transaction data rather than presenting incomplete figures as final.
